answer.rationale: The 18% cost mandate and 14-day renewal deadline create urgency, but the 94% assembly line utilization is a hard constraint—delivery risk cannot be absorbed. Memory_c4 demonstrates that renegotiating at renewal with the incumbent recovered real margin through benchmarking, achieving both price and terms improvement. Memory_c2 shows that switching to the low-cost vendor cut costs but created SLA miss risk across three of four quarters—unacceptable given current line buffer. Memory_c1 validates that incumbent renewal maintains integration stability with no migration work. Memory_c3 validates that a second source removes single-point failure risk, but given budget constraints and one-decision limit, a second source is deferred. Negotiating_terms leverages the incumbent relationship's proven stability while targeting the 18% reduction through market benchmarking. This preserves the 14-day deadline, avoids SLA-miss risk, and allows room for deferred decisions (second source, multi-year volume pricing per memory_c6) in the next cycle if negotiations fall short. Flagging downstream risk because incumbent has no guaranteed commitment below the 18% threshold; if negotiations fail, escalation to switch/defer becomes forced and high-risk.
